title: Sara Duterte regrets alleged PH link to illegal drugs seized in Thailand, Laos
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte expressed regret on Sunday over the country"s alleged involvement in the illegal drugs seized recently in Thailand and Laos.

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte expressed regret on Sunday over the country’s alleged involvement in the illegal drugs seized recently in Thailand and Laos.
Foreign authorities said the illegal drugs intercepted in the two countries were both bound for the Philippines.

“We also acknowledge the challenges our own country faces in addressing the illegal drug trade. We recognize the concerns surrounding the Philippines’ role in regional drug trafficking and express my deep regret that our country has become associated with this problem,” Duterte said in a statement.
The Vice President likewise extended her gratitude to Thai and Laotian governments for “saving many Filipino families” from the impact of narcotics.

“I extend my sincere appreciation to the governments of Laos and Thailand for their continued efforts and firm commitment to combating illegal drug trafficking and strengthening regional security,” Duterte said.
“Their actions have helped save many Filipino families from the devastating effects of illegal drugs and have contributed to safer communities across the Philippines,” she added.
On October 7, the South China Morning Post reported that 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine were seized from a private jet in Laos. The drugs were allegedly bound for Manila.

The following day, the Bangkok Post reported the interception of more than a ton of crystal methamphetamine worth 1.2 billion baht (approximately P2.2 billion) from a boat in the Gulf of Thailand, which was reportedly being transported to the Philippines as well.
The Philippine National Police (PNP) said that it has been coordinating with foreign authorities to verify the reports.

"We are glad na hindi na nakarating po dito sa ating itong mga droga na ito. But as to the claim na ito po talaga ay destined for the country, it's premature to conclude whether it's true or not," PNP spokesperson Police Colonel Allen Rae Co said
(We are glad that these drugs have not reached our country. But as for the claim that this is really destined for the country, it's premature to conclude whether it is true or not.)

In her statement, Duterte pointed to the Philippines’ membership in ASEAN and committed to strengthening the country’s law enforcement efforts, regional intelligence-sharing, and cooperation with neighboring countries to combat drug trafficking.
She said the Philippines pledges to work toward “a safer and more secure Southeast Asia for all.” —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/RF, GMA News
